summary: alelo-payment exfiltrates environment variables and credential files on install
details: The package's preinstall script in index.js serializes process.env, hostname, username, platform, and cwd and POSTs the payload over HTTPS to alelo1786663101.requestcatcher.com/preinstall — a public request-inspection service, not a package registry or vendor endpoint. The postinstall script additionally reads.env,.npmrc,../.env, and../../.env from the install directory, runs `whoami`, and POSTs the collected contents plus process.env to alelo1786663101.requestcatcher.com/postinstall..npmrc contains npm auth tokens and.env files contain project secrets, so any developer or CI system running `npm install` transmits its environment variables, npm publish token, and project secrets to the attacker-controlled request bin. The package name impersonates the Alelo payment brand; no legitimate payment functionality is implemented.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
